card.name: Words just before an exact count
card.fires_on: Small words that sit right before a number or amount, such as "exactly one", "a total of", "1 patient each", "just over", "one or two". The pole is strongest where the next word states an exact quantity.

modes.label: Total or exact amount
modes.description: Words like "exactly", "total of" and "from" that lead into a stated quantity or duration.
modes.example: Therapy must continue for a total<< of>> 60 days.

modes.label: Counts of patients
modes.description: "each" after a small number of patients in adverse event reports.
modes.example: Diplopia, mydriasis, and unequal pupillary size occurred in 1 patient<< each>> in the Unituxin/RA group

modes.label: Approximate quantity words
modes.description: Words like "just" or "two" in rough counts, and "mg" after a dose number.
modes.example: Of the more than 300,000 people who filled out the questionnaire,<< just>> over 1,000 --

card.writes: It suppresses words meaning "at least" (mostly Chinese), so it steers away from minimum-amount phrasing after a quantity lead-in.
card.plain: It fires on little words that come right before a number, like "a total of" or "1 patient each".
